JFC, istg this game is trying hard to make you rage against it and throw your controller at the screen. I mean come on, day and night cycle and limited days to prep before your next main task? 1. Polisi tidak se agrersif di NFS Heat, namun disini saat mereka interupsi balapan targeting nya bias dan hanya menarget kita seolah bot lain gak ada di pandangan mereka
2. Sistem rubberbanding yang bobrok, di game ini tidak peduli berapapun power yang dimiliki mobil anda akan menemukan momen dimana bot dengan power kecil yang tertinggal jauh melakukan overtake kepada kalian, yang mana hal ini konyol banget.
3. Sistem tier nya kaku banget, kita dipaksa mengikuti alur dengan mobil sesuai tier yang ada
4. Handling mobil sangat susah untuk akrab, berbeda dengan nfs heat yang handling nya lebih mudah, di game ini karakteristik handling benar benar susah di tebak, saat main benar benar terasa arcade tapi di waktu yang sama juga terasa seperti sim racing, kesalahan kontrol gas atau rem akan buat mobil spin, belum lagi Handbrake di game ini sangat tidak konsisten daya rem nya untuk melahap tikungan tajam
5. sistem Buy-In benar benar buat grinding sedikit menantang, mengingat rubberband membuat balapan di difficulty apapun susah, hasil yang didapat juga tidak bersih karena adanya Buy-In di awal.
6. Sangat sayang seribu sayang game ini sebenarnya seri NFS baru yang memiliki versi native PS5, tapi game ini tidak mendukung adanya haptik dari dualsense, sehingga akan susah bagi kita untuk merasakan feeling grip mobil melalui respon yang keluar dari dualsense

This is a review from someone who didn't grow up playing NFS, so I won't be comparing it to the other games. Firstly, I like cars. I like this game (so far). You can customise not just the car visuals, but the engine inside it and parts that upgrade your car's performance, although that part is locked til after the Prologue which only takes a few hours. The sounds are satisfying, the visuals are satisfying too - I personally like the cartoon style of the characters and the graffiti driving effects when you drift. I feel like it adds some character into your builds and a vibe of "street racing with graffiti" which fits the anti authority theme of the game. The story could be better. Well, the story isn't so bad but it's more the dialogue. Feels slightly cringey at times but bearable IMO. 

Is it a realistic racing sim? No. Is it meant to be? No. It's an arcade racer with a certain vibe and visual theme, one that some people will love and some people will hate. I like the driving in this game. It can be a bit janky at times I will admit but for the most part, going 200mph in a widebody Ford Mustang Boss and then drifting round the corner like you're Ken Block is enough for me to overlook the bad points in the game.

There's a difficulty setting - I keep it at a medium level. AI seems like it's better than you at times, other times you manage to secure a good overtake and it feels great. Running from police is fun and nerve wrecking at the same time, especially when your car is deemed "risky" or "challenging" for the heat level you have acquired.

If you're a hardcore old school NFS gamer then I can't guarantee you will like it. But as someone who is into cars and into customising them and then racing away from the rozzers (cops) like it's Fast and Furious, I recommend it :)

(Also, specs are attached. Game runs perfectly fine for me with controller except the odd bug here and there.)

claims.claim: Reviewers note that character dialogue and the overall story are cringeworthy or poorly written.

citations.review_text:
Need For Speed Unbound *is* good, despite what some might have you think. There are some who seem to forget that this series has always been gloriously campy and never taken itself seriously - it's basically just Hot Wheels for the grown-ups - and they are shrieking like wounded infants because the dialogue isn't exactly high art. Some of the characters are cringe-inducing, of this I am in accord, but veterans of the series will remember that even Most Wanted was incredibly goofy in this regard (remember "EVERYONE!!!", anybody?).

If you are looking for a racing game, then the first, second and last question you should be asking: is NFS Unbound a good *racing* game, first and foremost? If that question isn't at the very forefront of your mind when making your mind up about whether to play this, then what are you even looking for to begin with? For me, the answer is yes. This is a good racing game, and I do have great fun with it even when I get totally obliterated by level 400 online veterans in every other race.

This series has long-suffered the burden of being under the greedy thumb of EA, and its God-awful monetization reflects that. But in spite of this, Criterion were genuinely willing to take gambles with the cell-shaded character models and anime-adjacent art in an era where big-name franchises are terrified of their own shadows and unwilling to take risks. Some don't like what they did, and they're perfectly entitled to that opinion, but I personally love it. And if nothing else, I would far rather watch a studio throw themselves off a creative cliff than for me to fork over $90 for the exact same grey-scale slate that every other studio has been churning out since time out of mind. What's been slowly dying in the gaming industry has been creative experimentation, and even if you don't like this particular choice in outcome, the spirit of the act itself should still be encouraged nevertheless.

It saddens me then to say that, somehow, this game is still ver…

Honestly lowkey a pretty decent racing game. The sense of speed is done quite well. The old story of going from nothing to something never gets old. The only gripes are the repeated races, the blatant cheating the AI will do to catch up to you, the cops screwing you over mid race, and the horrible writing (i still found myself enjoying it sometimes and getting used to how corny it was). Honestly a fun little 6.5/10 game. Its 100% worth the $5 when its on sale.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the singleplayer campaign features a rigid weekly schedule format with limited restart attempts.

citations.review_text:
[h1] What I liked [/h1]
[olist]
[*]The arcade controls are really fun. The burst NOS mechanic fun to use. You can also perform very well on grip builds if thats what you prefer.
[*]I guess the multiplayer is fun.
[*]The car customization is great as always.
[*]In singleplayer, you only have limited restart attempts and have to bet your own money to take part in races. I understand that it doesn't vibe with some people but I liked the way it increased the stakes. 
[*]Many people hate the effects but I personally love them, they are the whole reason I bought the game. You can turn them off if you want. The overall graphics are also very beautiful.
[*]Overall I found the game really addictive and without exageration I could not stop playing it these past few days. Had an absolute blast.
[/olist]
Then why not recommended? Cause this game deserves it for many reasons. But I would not recommend this for the garbage handling alone.

[h1] What I disliked (rant alert) [/h1]
The horribly cringe dialogue and story. I will however say, that the light hearted political takes and the general wokeness made me appreciate it more. I got the feeling that the writers wrote all that with passion and it made the game feel like it had a soul. I could be wrong though, maybe the whole thing is indeed coorporate slop.

Not a lot of variety in tracks. They made an entire open world map for this game and I can't help but feel they didn't fully utilize it.

Inconsistent physics, general randomness with traffic and cops in races made for many frustrating moments.

The car handling is really fun but also very inconsistent. Sometimes, I would try to drift and the car just wouldn't do it for whatever reason (I promise it was not skill issue) so I made habit of pressing the input twice and that fixed it for me. Sometimes you take a turn and it does a grip turn, other times it starts drifting for whatever reason (yes I was on even road in both cases). Sometimes I would drift and the car would turn t…

The Handling is terrible.
The Characters are cringe and annoying, every, and i mean [u] every [/u] dialog contains some forced witty, "funny" comment.
There's limited restarts.
The weekly schedule format makes the career way too restricted and rigid, you can't really go at your own pace.
The opponents and cops are way too rubberband-y.
For some godforsaken reason some idiot at criterion thought it would be a good idea to put chromatic aberration on the HUD, making it look blurry constantly.
Once you have the highest wanted level (which happens very quickly) the cops will chase you during and after almost every single race.

It's bad, it's just bad.

A ton of cars that outpace you by three kilometers, created by third-party programs with added properties or transferred to a class where they would be impossible to place under the game's default conditions, or, using vulnerabilities, they teleport half a kilometer away. the game is pretty good but a too much cheater

I have over 100 hours in Need for Speed Unbound, and overall I really enjoyed my time with it. The game's unique visual style, driving mechanics, art direction, and especially the Lockdown mode kept me coming back for more. Car performance customization is also surprisingly deep, allowing players to fine-tune their builds for different racing styles.

That said, this game won't appeal to everyone. If you're looking for a classic story-focused Need for Speed experience, Unbound may not be what you're after. However, if you enjoy arcade racing, stylish visuals, customization, and online competition, there's a lot to love here.

One of the best parts of my experience was meeting some great people online and racing together. Unfortunately, since the developers have stopped supporting the game, hackers have become a major problem. I've reported several players through EA Support, but many of them continue to ruin lobbies by using accleration mod, cheating, and disrupting gameplay. The lack of effective action against these players is easily the game's biggest flaw.

Despite its issues, I still think Need for Speed Unbound is a good game that deserves a chance, especially for fans of arcade racing and unique artistic direction.
